lines.x: You hear something?
It's a busy street, it's all something.
What I'm more worried about is this smell.

The goods got all packed up, and stashed in the cellar. Shouldn't be any smell at all...
Hah, well, if you find anything loose, I could go for a taste.
Don't even think about it. They say this stuff's the cream of the crop.
But that scent is makin' me wanna quit this job.
You wanna quit workin', or wanna quit work here?
What's the difference?
Either way, we're stuck roamin' this street, keepin' watch and hopin' nobody comes lookin' for trouble.
That red paint from last night ain't washin' out. Once we get paid, I'm buyin' a new coat for my ride.
Suit yourself. I'm savin' my share. The company's gonna need more guys for later.
What's with the look?
Nuova Volsinii really is a goddamn miracle, turnin' a Sicilian like you into a responsible businessman. This fat Kazimierzian pays way more than Antonio ever did, right?
How was I supposed to know runnin' a taxi company had all these costs?
Even drivin' a taxi's a lot more exciting than patrollin' this street, though.
What kind of dipshit with too much time on his hands would try to mess up this 'Red Wine Championship', anyway? I got nothin'.
Fuhgeddaboudit. We're done with this street, let's head back to the theater.
Y'know, why'd the Kazimierzian come to us with this event security job anyway?
Beats me. Maybe a referral from some kind soul.
Ladies and gentlemen, if I may occupy a moment of your time.

The lighting in the theater is almost a little too bright, as if trying to light up every face in the building. A well-dressed businessman stands in the center of the stage, lightly tapping the glass of red wine in his hand.
The crisp note is not loud, but it still gets the guests to quiet down.
I know you're all looking forward to the wine and the music, and to the moments ahead that will be worth remembering.
But we'll get to that. First, I'd like to say a few words: hosting the Red Wine Championship here in this city means so much to us.
Nuova Volsinii is a promise of order. And ever since we selected this place for our competition, that promise has been proven beyond doubt.
Wine takes time.
And time demands stability.
The Kazimierzian businessman continues on once the applause dies down. He talks of the year of the vintage, how it was made, and of course, intercity cooperation and logistics systems.
Every word falls into place, with nary a syllable wasted.
Naturally, without the support of Nuova Volsinii City Hall, this championship might never have come together so quickly.
It is our honor to be working with you, Mayor Bellone.
Nuova Volsinii welcomes all foreign partners willing to abide by our city's laws.
So long as you are here to do respectable business, nothing will stand in your way.
Haha, of course, of course.
I'm not here to flatter you.
In Nuova Volsinii, I have no fear of the famiglie trying to get a hand in my business, no need to search for any 'hidden meanings' in the deals I sign.
Such clarity in business is truly priceless.
It sounds like you have a very positive opinion of our city.
Exactly, that is why we wish to bring the finest wines here, alongside some much-needed cooperation.
In that case, we find ourselves honored.
We're still waiting here, when are we getting started?
Yeah, I wanna see how good Kazimierzian wine really is!
A few rude voices force their way out of the crowd, and begin to spread throughout the audience. But under the bright lights, the businessman's face shows no signs of displeasure.
Haha, I suppose I've droned on too long and tested our guests' patience.
Then I would like to invite Nuova Volsinii's famed orchestra to the stage! Their performance shall serve as the opening ceremony for the championship finals!
As the lights dim, Czarek takes the opportunity to accompany Leontuzzo off the stage, to appreciate the performance from some nearby corner.
Leontuzzo, however, does not look to the stage. With no glaring lights to blind him, he can see the man calmly walking up to him.
Mi dispiace. My associates aren't used to this sort of thing, so they got a little excited.
It's fine. There'll probably be plenty more events like this coming to Nuova Volsinii.
Guess I'd better teach them to behave soon, then.
And who might this gentleman be?
Signor Demetri Bellone, a local wine merchant, also participating in the competition.
Ah, your reputation precedes you—the young, promising head of Saluzzo Vino.

A pleasure. Though there's one thing I've been meaning to ask—
Everyone is here tonight just for the tasting session, right?
Haha, of course, of course.
The question of a wine's quality is ultimately answered by the tongue.
Good.
I was worried this championship would be decided by whose background was cleaner or who had the nicer story to tell.
Haha, the story behind a wine is important, but if the wine cannot stand on its own two feet, then even the prettiest words will not prop it up for long.
You're right. I'm sure the victor will be crowned based solely on its flavor.
It sounds like you won't be disappointed, even if your wine doesn't make it to the finals.
You're a funny man, Mayor Bellone.
You look the very picture of a businessman now.
Were you hoping I wouldn't be?
I've heard Kazimierzians have great faith in 'fair competition'. I'm eager to see it for myself tonight.
But I have the feeling the real results will make themselves known very quickly.
Haha, sounds like I have something to look forward to. To witness a fair competition in Nuova Volsinii, a city no longer bound by the old rules—
Why, that's the entire reason we're here.
You hear something?
You asked me that when we were heading out the door.
What could be makin' noise down in the cellar, unless it's someone stealin' wine?
This is all the wine they got for the competition? Just this one row?
Yeah. I gues' the guests get to drink the entries once it's over. You'd hafta be missing a few screws to try n' steal some right now.
So can we drink some?
Yeah, sure, lemme pour you a glass. Of course we can't, idiota.
Shame.
You said you wanted to try some, right? If you pour yourself a glass, I won't snitch.
As soon as the words leave his mouth, footsteps ring out from between some shelves around the corner.
A Caprinae with a hood obscuring his face lowers his head as he walks through the shelves, heading for the stairs leading up. Soon enough, he has left the cellar.
He's gone.
Probably didn't hear us...
From that distance? He wouldn't have even seen us. Long horns like that, gotta be a Caprinae. I figure he's with the orchestra.
Why would an orchestra guy be down here at a time like this? They're goin' on in a minute, right?
Maybe he's just calming his nerves. You got your own tics, y'know? Every time you're holdin' your piece, you keep scratchin' at the safety with your nail.
Cazzata, I ain't done that in years—
Gambino shuts up the moment he hears more agitated footsteps.
Another Caprinae appears from the shadows, following the echoing footsteps of the orchestra member from earlier. She, too, quickly leaves the cellar.
This time, both Capone and Gambino saw suspicion on the blonde girl's face.
Hey, I know that ragazza. She's the daughter of the lady who runs the orchestra, gave me my security pass.
When was the last time I saw this many Caprinae in Siracusa?
I figure the whole orchestra is from Leithanien.
What, you gonna say something like 'just like the Sicilians'?
Nah. Was just thinkin' how Nuova Volsinii's gettin' too crowded. Kuranta, Caprinae, hell, if I came across an Ægir on the street, I wouldn't even bat an eye anymore.
I'm hopin' for fewer strange-looking passengers through the door.
Let's do one more lap around the cellar. The performance oughta be startin' up there.
The orchestra takes the stage, and the lights dim once more.

The strings begin with restrained, gentle tones. Soon, they are joined by the woodwinds. Though the melody can hardly be called brash, it serves as a vector to reveal the notes in their most perfect forms.
The audience lifts their glasses, slowly swaying them along to the music. Leontuzzo sits in the front row, watching his neighbor Demetri refuse yet another glass of red wine from an attendant.
You come to a wine tasting and don't taste the wine.
I just don't have an appreciation for the smell of that Kazimierzian red wine.
You got here earlier than I expected.
I was invited, so I'm not allowed to drop by at the last second. Otherwise, it'll look like I'm back to my old habits.
Aren't you in the same situation, Mayor Bellone?
Whenever you say 'old habits', it always makes me feel like you're bragging about the progress you've made.
I'll take that as a compliment. You know me. I was never any good at picking out the condemnations between the praise.
Leontuzzo does not answer. He simply turns his head away from the stage and back toward Demetri, his eyes falling on the bowtie around his neck.
It's been too long since they last met. He's not sure just how much of Demetri's current business-like demeanor is sincere.
You look like a real businessman today, Demetri.
Not to your liking?
There are a lot of things to my liking, but that doesn't mean I'm not worried.
What about Nuova Volsinii? Is it going the way you hoped it would? Worried about the city and the people who scurry around it?
It's growing as I expected.
You're the same as you ever were. You talk about order, but your eyes are fixed on the people—Hey, my hands are clean. What, scared I'm gonna take something from you?
What scares me is you treating the city like your kitchen table. Give it a flip, and everything on top will come crashing down to the ground.
Then you'd better watch me closely, Leon. The closer you stick to me, the harder it'll be for me to mess up.
The Kazimierizian businessman beside them is clearly in a good mood.
He stands up as the performance ends, lightly applauding as he signals the attendants to prepare the next step.
I have to say, I love how you Nuova Volsiniese know when to applaud, and when to stay quiet.
It's a rare thing. Most places, people make a ruckus when they should be silent, and stay quiet when they should be clapping up a storm.
I'd like to thank the orchestra for their marvelous performance. I'd also like to invite tonight's judge to come and witness our competition.
A musician from Leithanien and a guest of this fair city, Frau Paola.
As a woman unaffiliated with any wine dealer or famiglia, I think there's no one more suited for the job.
The conductor on the stage gives a graceful nod to the audience, before being guided by an attendant to the table of red wines at the front.
Buonasera, everyone.
I know only how to play music and conduct an orchestra, so I'm not very good at offering praise, or pretty descriptions, but since I'm judging the finals, I promise—
I will sample them all with care, then say what I feel as I drink them, truthfully.
Haha, that's exactly why we chose you.
Pretty descriptions? No, what we need are honest assessments.
He lifts his hand, beckoning the attendants to fill three wine glasses from three decanters.
Now then, let's begin.
The three finalists come from different wineries and different terroirs, and they each have their own 'ambitions'.
The rules are simple: no looking at the labels, no listening to any stories, just pure flavor. If you will, Frau Paola.
The tall musician nods, a serious look on her face as she lifts the first glass. She sniffs, sips, swallows, and stops.
The first glass... sticks strictly to the standard.
The aroma is unassertive; it does not rush the mouth. The fruity flavor is front-loaded, and quickly restrained.
You can tell that it avoids making any mistakes, not letting any one flavor linger for too long. All in all, a harmonious package.
This is a wine I could offer to guests without worry.
The second glass is, hmm, very much like the locals.
The alcohol makes itself known quickly, but not in an irritating way, and without any sharp sensations.
It's a little bold when entering the mouth, with a direct sourness, the type that wouldn't ask for your opinion beforehand.
It is the third glass that Paola savors the slowest. She takes a sip, but does not immediately swallow, letting the red wine linger on the tip of her tongue for a moment.
The third glass...
There's no brashness at the beginning, but the layering and the structure are very clear. It's not a crowd-pleasing sort of wine...
It's as if... it doesn't care if you enjoy it or not. It's not going to try and win you over. It knows its own path, and it'll walk it to the end.
It has attitude. An attitude I happen to like.
Czarek turns to the audience and raises his hand, as if he were already standing atop the podium.
Now, Frau Paola, if you would pick which of the three glasses you believe is most worth remembering—
The third, naturally.
Czarek is practically already reaching out for the bottle behind the third glass. His voice is more excited than before, but he maintains his composure.
Well, I think we all heard her.
This wine is—
You'd best check the label again.
Otherwise, things might end up rather embarrassing for you.
Pardon...?
Czarek freezes. He slowly looks down at the bottle. The moment he gets a clear look at the label, the smile on his face dies.
But only for a moment. A moment so short that almost nobody can react. Once it passes, his rictus grin is plastered back onto his face.
...It seems tonight's first surprise arrived earlier than I expected.
Like you said, no leaning on stories, just the wine itself.
I really must wonder, though, how did a bottle of 'Golden Prairie' transform into a wine that isn't on the list of finalists?
Oh? I guess even Kazimierz's legendary business management systems aren't free from little mistakes like registration errors.
Haha, yes, just a little mistake!
Let's all give a warm round of applause to the winner, Saluzzo Vino!
Your wine has earned our most stringent, yet most objective praise.
Grazie mille. I'm glad the words 'fair competition' still apply tonight.
It's a good thing for everyone involved.
Haha, a good thing indeed.
If the winner were always predetermined, then business would be dreadfully boring. And the very reason I came to Nuova Volsinii was to get away from boring business.
Let us toast! To the champion, a local winery—and to this fair city!
Salute.
The attendants begin refilling the guests' glasses. Applause rings out once more, more enthusiastic than before.
Applause that includes Leontuzzo's clapping.
Not going to toast me, Leon?
You know my palate isn't as refined as yours. Won't you introduce your winning wine before the toast?
Hah... If you insist.
This isn't a wine that needs much introduction. It's not trying to impress anyone, or to prove anything with the first sip.

It's most suited for when the dinner table's almost cleared out, and most things worth saying have been said, but you're not quite ready to leave yet. That's when you notice there's still a glass of this left.
It will be your final safeguard, making sure your words don't spill out onto the floor. It will remind you of the past, and make it easier to reach an agreement.
If you think this is exactly the wine you need, then it's already done its job.
This wine... has some grand ambitions.
So it does. It's like what Frau Paola just said. It follows the path of its choosing, without caring whether you like it or not.
Since it chose this road, I've got nothing to say about whether I like it.
Demetri smiles, but does not answer. He simply raises his glass, giving it a gentle clink against Leontuzzo's.
Before the clink can fade away, a light, incongruent cough makes itself heard from the other side of the stage.
Paola's hand stops in midair, the glass between her fingers trembling ever so slightly, as the wine leaves irregular streaks on the glass.
...Sorry.
*cough* *COUGH*!
She wants to finish speaking, but all her subconscious lets her do is steady her breathing. Her second cough comes out sharp. She tries to lower her voice, but she cannot cover it up completely.
The blonde girl who is always by her side is the first to notice the look on her face. Paola lifts her hand to prop herself up against the table, but she can no longer stand steady.
The glass falls from her hand, letting out a muffled thump as it falls onto the carpet.
She falls forward, her body unable to support itself.
Some cry out, some rise to their feet, and some reflexively take a step back.
Before the attendants can rush to the scene, she has already collapsed by the table, no longer breathing, her lips taking on an odd hue under the lights.
The blonde girl babbles things like 'Paola!' and 'Help her!'.
The smile instantly disappears from Demetri's face. Czarek stays standing, but does not speak.
With the flash of chaos now over, the theater sinks into a surreal silence.
Moments ago, they were toasting things like 'fairness', 'dignity' and 'victory'.
But now, nobody reaches for the wine on the table.
The disturbance did not last long. Thanks to the mayor and some municipal staff among the attendees, the situation is quickly reined in.
Many people simply stand there, unsure if they should move closer, or leave.
Please remain calm, everyone.
The medics are already on their way. Before we clean up, I would like to ask you all to work with our security staff, and not act on your own.
Mayor Bellone, I must emphasize to both you and our guests that the wines underwent a strict auditing process.
None of us wished to see anything like this happen.
But we cannot allow rumors to spread.
Leontuzzo stands to the side. He does not answer immediately. He looks at the table the attendants have moved away from the rest, and then at Demetri, who still stands in the same spot.
Demetri says nothing. He does not approach, nor back away. He gently puts the wine glass he is holding down, which lets out the lightest of clinks as its foot meets the table.
The noise prompts Czarek to continue.
Something unexpected happened at the wine tasting.
The label on the wine bottle does not match our registry.
I don't believe this is an act of malice. But under the present circumstances, anything outside the standard process needs a clear explanation.
The crowd's gazes wash over the scene like a wave, before inevitably landing on Demetri.
If you're waiting for me to explain, then I'm afraid I'll have to disappoint.
I'm as shocked as anyone else here that something like this could happen.
As for the bottle of wine, I was only responsible for its flavor, and getting it to the theater on time.
Anything else is none of my business.
You are the young, promising head of a winery, but also the young, promising head of a gang, aren't you? You might be uninvolved, but you have plenty of minions to get involved for you.
According to many eyewitnesses, Frau Paola suddenly fell to the ground after taking another drink from the bottle of Saluzzo Vino red that mysteriously appeared.
What sort of grudge was there between you two that led to this?
Was it not enough that your wine won my championship? Did you want to ruin my business as well?
Or do you famiglia bosses have your feuds and conspiracies in which you trample over us ordinary folk?
Signor Czarek.
We do not know all the facts yet. Nuova Volsinii has its own procedures, and this incident will be investigated accordingly.
Since it was a public incident, the police will be involved. Before they announce their results, nobody, neither individual nor body corporate, should be making premature statements.
Naturally, of course.
We also hope the truth will come to light quickly. Otherwise, people will lose trust in Kazimierzian reds, perhaps even local Nuova Volsiniese reds as well.
Mayor Bellone, death is not a welcome guest at my Red Wine Championship, I suspect at any wine meet.
And I would prefer not to hear streetcorner rumors about how our Kazimierzian competition was drawn into famiglia struggles, how we were powerless to resist... Things like that.
Surely you are aware that we businessmen of Kazimierz, along with our counterparts from Leithanien, Columbia, and nations even further afield...
Are only here in Nuova Volsinii because of what kind of promises you've made.
Czarek lowered his voice, but the reporters and cameramen invited to the venue to capture the championship seem to have heard every word.
The cameras are flashing much more frequently than they were.
Under their glare, Demetri steps forward.
If you need me to comply with the investigation, then I won't run and hide.
I will halt all activities until the results are in.
Demetri! As I said, I am begging everyone to avoid any rash actions until after things have been cleared up.
Well, I appear to be the prime suspect right now. So I will stay where I should stay, and let the police do all the investigating they want.
I ask that you do it all in accordance with the standard procedures you mentioned, Mayor Bellone.
...Right.
I'll make the arrangements.
Does City Hall still need time to send the police? No need to trouble them, then. My own hired security can escort Signor Bellone home.
Leontuzzo was looking at the red-haired Lupo's face earlier, trying to see if he could spot anything.
The moment the wine glass fell to the floor, the smile on Demetri's face vanished. Now, it has returned, just barely perceptible.
But it is only a smile. Leontuzzo is not sure if he should interpret it as 'I won't embarrass you', 'I believe you can figure this out', or 'I made plans for this long ago'.
Before he can finish deciphering it, Demetri is led to the exit, flanked by Capone and Gambino. As he passes by, their gazes meet for the shortest of instants, before they are separated.
The flashing lights of the reporters' cameras cascade across Demetri's face.
Leontuzzo instinctively turns away, composing himself before turning back to the foreigner who has seized this chance to pile on the pressure and demand more from him.
How'd you put it?
'I beg your forgiveness, Don Demetri. Did the rope chafe you?'
Nearly died tryin' not to laugh.
He's the real power behind the Saluzzos in Nuova Volsinii, and the new don of the Bellones. Can't hurt to show him a little respect.
Not to mention the tip he gave us—Hell, can't even call a wad of cash this big a 'tip'.
A don, but he still got pulled into that foreign moneyman's scheme.
You think the Kazimierzian pulled one over on him?
I'm tellin' you, I think he spiked that drink on purpose, just to get in the middle of all this... Remember when we dragged him outta the theater, man was as cool as a cucumber.
Wise guys like him, who were born into the famiglie, they're good at this kinda scheming, and used to it too.
Who the hell knows, man? I don't give a shit.
This is Nuova Volsinii, not Sicilia. You and I both know how stupid dons can look when they fall from the top.
Hey, you think those reporters got a photo of our taxi company's sign when we were takin' him out of that place?
Buy a paper tomorrow and check for yourself.
Maybe they'll only get the 'Siciliano' part of it, now that'd be a joke.
What, mad? Fine, I'll drop it.
Nah... it's not that. I just suddenly got the feeling like maybe Nuova Volsinii is still a Siracusan city.
There's been a lotta change here, but in the end, maybe nothin's changed at all.
Or maybe, when you push somethin' that's never changed down a new track, some other stuff's gotta start poppin' up.
Scusa, Bettina, I'd love to help you, but... I'm running a small business here too, y'know.
Those bottles I got from you last time are still on my wine rack, gathering dust. Why not go ask at the corner store?
Right, I'll go do that! Grazie, Zio Paolo!
...I already asked, actually. Nobody wants any.
I've gotta move all this out of the way first. If I keep standing around here like a fool, I'll affect Zio Paolo's business.
Hup—Wh-Wh-Whoaaaaawha?!
Careful!
That was close... Here, hold it tight now.
Th-Thank you, signorina.
Man, this is heavy, no wonder a little kid like you couldn't carry it right. What's in this—
Oh, it's Verdi.
You know it?
I'm Bettina, and this is from the Verdi Winery where my nonno works! The winery's got decades of history behind it! Would you like to buy a bottle, signorina?
...I see.
Bettina, right? I guess it's fate I've bumped into you, so let's make friends.
I'm Tosia. Here, my card.
Wow, cool, a business card! Sorry, I don't have one... Huh?
Kazimierz Golden Prairie Winery, Nuova Volsinii branch... sales representative?

I'm betting that before long, it'll say 'Senior Relationship Manager'...
But that's the thing. I'm afraid we're competitors, so I won't be buying your wine.
Now, if you wouldn't mind scooching out of the way, little Miss Bettina, I have a great deal to make with Signor Paolo.
You just arrived in Nuova Volsinii, and you've already talked the locals into some huge deals! Excellent work!
Come, Tosia! Today, we give our top sales rep the welcome feast she deserves!
You're too kind, Wujek Czarek!
You've been busy getting the Red Wine Championship ready, so of course you didn't have time for dinner. I just hope I haven't been much trouble.
Not at all! I'm a lucky man, getting an experienced sales girl to join us at Golden Prairie!
But I heard you were doing well at the Krzywy Domek Department Store. Why Nuova Volsinii all of a sudden?
It's... a long story.
Let me guess, it's something to do with that... 'Silverlance Pegasus corruption case' that's got Kawalerielki all abuzz lately?
Though Czarek lowered his voice, the mention of the case has Tosia jerking her head upwards.
How did you...?
I was told that the G.C.C. sent agents to Krzywy Domek and took one of your managers a few days ago. Your old manager, even.
Guess there's no hiding anything from you. She took good care of me, but... one of her relatives is a Silverlance Pegasus.
It was a point of pride, but once the G.C.C. started poking around... Whenever they can't directly move against the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi, they take the people around them for 'questioning'.
And more and more people keep getting involved in the case. Some poor souls get the entire book thrown at them, even though anyone with eyes can see they're totally innocent...
If normal folk like us get pulled into this kind of trouble, how're we supposed to resist giants like the G.C.C.?
That's why I thought it'd be better to come here and expand—
Tosia, Golden Prairie would not have grown this large in Nuova Volsinii without behind-the-scenes support from the G.C.C.
When the big shots show some initiative and want to expand their horizons, that is a good thing for businesspeople like us.
...You're right.
Let's not think too much about Kawalerielki while we're here.
Just keep your enthusiasm flowing and do a good job. When my business is growing, it's only good for you, no?
Then I'll thank you in advance, Wujek Czarek.
Clever girl. I won't belabor the point, then.
I've already ordered the food, just need to know what you want to drink.

Sorry for putting all that on you. Honestly, I'm not too good at handling wine.
Let me see...
Oh, right, I'm looking for a certain brown-colored soft drink. I think it's a local Siracusan brand, tastes like orange with a bit of bitterness?
Do you mean Chinotto, signorina? I am terribly sorry, but we don't carry that one.
Where did you even learn of that old beverage? Since we put out our soft drink line, the local brands have pretty much all died out.
Huh... Really?
Did you forget our slogan, Tosia? 'Nuova Volsinii, Vita Nuova'. Leave the retro nostalgia to the Leithanians.
How about some zero-proof sparkling water?
Haha, sure! Let's go with that, then.
Good, good. Oh, almost forgot. Come, I wanted to show this to you.
It's a... shelf display agreement?
Just a draft template. I was hoping to hear what our top sales representative thought before we deployed it.
It's very clear on the criteria, and the rewards are generous... There shouldn't be too many retailers who decline.
But if they do accept, it means they can only display our products while the agreement is in force.
Wouldn't an exclusivity clause like that create legal issues under local law?
There's nothing in the New Urban Management Act that says we can't have one.
The way I see it, those Lupos with their heads full of dreams and faith won't see any issues with it.
Czarek shrugs, a smile of victory on his face.
But it's you frontline employees who will be talking to the retailers, not me. I'm eager to see how you do, when the time comes, Tosia.
Thank you for waiting. Your zero-proof sparkling water, signorina.
Come, to Nuova Volsinii, and to vita nuova! Na zdrowie!
...I would never let you down, Wujek Czarek.

Na zdrowie!
Whew... I'm stuffed!
'Chef's Selection'... Seriously? Tiny portions and way too much fuss.
After shoving the last piece of pizza into her mouth, Tosia brushes the crumbs off her hands and continues her walk back to her place alongside the night breeze.
The street is lit up in vibrant colors by a chaotic mix of billboards, shining as bright as day. This nightscape is breathtaking, but it could not be more different from the Siracusa Tosia imagined.
...Shelf display agreement, more like shelf monopoly agreement.

It's going to get a whole lot of people fired, maybe even bankrupted, won't it? Like that kid from before. Once the agreement's signed, she won't be able to sell her wine, no matter how much legwork she puts in...
But it's got to be done. Those Victorians and Columbians aren't going to let an opportunity this big slip by, even if we did.
Hmm?
Oh? It's you, the lady from this morning.

How's it going? Manage to sell any...?
*sigh* You're still carrying the same bottles, aren't you?
Yeah...
You're a really good saleswoman, right, Signorina Tosia? Can you—
Nope.
Huh? But I didn't even get to ask...
You want me to teach you a trick or two, right? I can read it on your face. Anyway, no can do, no way.
But why?
The despondency and incomprehension on the girl's face force a long sigh out of Tosia.
How old are you, Bettina?
I'm ten next week.
Ten, huh... Alright, let me put this in a way you can understand.
Listen, I know having to make a living at your age isn't easy. If things were different, I wouldn't mind helping you out.
I only got to where I am today thanks to the help of others. A favor is an investment, not a cost.
But here's the problem: there's only so much wine one Nuova Volsinian can drink in a day.
You're selling Verdi, I'm selling Golden Prairie. We're business rivals, enemies even.

Of course, in a situation like this, some people would drop any cost-benefit analysis, and choose to help a helpless little kid like you... but that's not me.
Because I'm a woman with a heart of stone!
The business world is a battlefield! Helping your enemy is just stabbing yourself in the back!
I've set my mind on flying up the ranks and living the good life, and I'm not going to go soft on my foe just because she's a kid! You got that?!
Got it...
Good! I'm off, then. You keep at it.
...Was I too harsh on her?
Can't blame me for it. That black-hearted uncle of mine is obviously trying to use pie-in-the-sky promises to trick me into doing his dirty work.
If I want to find my footing here, I don't have time to get involved in other people's business.
But... she's not crying, is she? Let's just turn around and get a quick look, just one look...
Hm...
(Droops head, as if grieving)
(Grabs hold of bridge railing)
(Stands on top of railing)
(As if about to jump—)
Whoa, whoa, WHOA! WAIT, WAIT! DON'T JUST THROW YOUR LIFE AWAY LIKE THAT—!
Wha—?!
Made it... Good thing I got quick reflexes...
Kids these days have no mental fortitude! I'll teach you, okay?!

Seriously, even when my performance was in the gutter, and I was homeless and living under a bridge, eating thrown-out fries, things weren't that bad!
You're young, you've got plenty of time ahead of you! As long as you're alive, there's hope! Even if things are hard now, you need to believe things will get bet...
ter...
Why are you looking at me like that?
I think you misunderstood something, Signorina Tosia. I was trying to save Pane.
...Pane?
Over there, on the other side of the railing. It's so naughty, wandering off like that...
Woof!
So you weren't trying to...?
Haha, thank goodness. I guess I looked real stupid trying to calm you down just now, worried as I was.
But even if you were trying to save it, you didn't need to go over the railing, you know! That's dangerous!
But my arms aren't long enough...
Alright, fine, out of the way! You better not bite me, Pane!
Sono molto grata, Bettina! If you hadn't brought my bambino back to me, why, I don't know what to do!
We'll head back home now. Say ciao to Bettina, Pane.
Okay! Ciao, Signora Bianca! Ciao, Pane!
Huh? Wait, aren't you going to ask her?
Ask her what?
About the wine! I feel like getting sales through personal connections is rather high-cost-low-efficiency, but any port in a storm. Definitely beats starving.
Didn't you help her find Pane so she would buy your wine?
Huh?
Don't tell me you did it out of the goodness of your heart.
Am I misunderstanding something? Is your family not in big trouble? Does it not matter if this stuff sells?
No, of course it matters! I just want to help sell the wine. Nonno says sales have been getting worse and worse lately, and if we can't make enough this month, the winery will have to close...
What should I do? You said you'd teach me.
What? When did I say that—
Kids these days have no mental fortitude! I'll teach you, okay?!
Oh. I guess I did. Though I thought you were going to... Ahem.
I'm not trying to wiggle out of what I said, but take a good look at your product. Cheap, local wines like your Verdi are the worst performers in the current market.

Outdated production facilities, careless cost control, old-fashioned marketing... While Golden Prairie offers some better-quality budget wines, and they are only half the price. Only a fool would pick the other option.
The winery your nonno works for is doomed. My advice to him is to start looking for a new job sooner rather than later.
But the adults all say there's no such thing as an unsellable product, only salespeople who can't sell it.
I know Verdi is hard to sell... Is it so bad that not even you could sell it, Signorina Tosia?
First you trick me into giving you advice, then you go for a psychological tactic? You've got moves.
Trick...?
But I won't fall for it, hehe.

I don't have to get mixed up in your problems to prove myself. I'm last year's sales star at the Krzywy Domek Department Store, and the future top salesperson at Golden Prairie. There's nothing I can't sell...
That's right, absolutely nothing! Alright, since you've talked your way this far, allow me to teach you a thing or two!
With my secret sales techniques, forget selling a few bottles, you'll be selling crates by the dozen!
...Alright, tell me the story. Why is it you haven't sold a single bottle yet?
Sorry, I know how hard it was for you to find free time to teach me, but I... *sniff*
I can afford a day off, I've built enough of a lead on second place. Gotta leave myself some room for improvement next month...
The important thing is, you're my apprentice, how can you be getting stuck like this?! Are you really doing things the way I taught you?
I did my best to use the words you taught me, but...
But?
Things like 'the wine is full-bodied, with exquisite balance and a lively zing'. I don't understand what they mean at all, so how am I supposed to pretend I do when talking to people?
And then saying things like our wine 'comes from a winery with deep historical roots'... We just use grapes from our own vineyard. Isn't this misleading?

Nonno says we should put ourselves in other people's shoes, and be sincere when dealing with them. That way, everyone will trust us. It's the only way to get a good deal that everyone's happy with, so I... I...
*sigh*... I knew it.
Listen to me. Your playbook is outdated.

You're being sincere, but other people aren't necessarily going to be sincere back. Gullible idiots get swindled and lose everything. Even if they put it all on the line to make some cash, they just burn themselves out.
You'll see, when you find yourself in a desperate situation. Then you'll look around and see no one ready to lend you a hand. Sincerity means nothing in the face of profit.
You can't entrust your survival to anyone else. We need to be smart, or we'll get gobbled up. You hear me?
I... I don't know...
The sight of the girl with her head lowered, clutching at her clothes, makes Tosia decide to lighten up a bit.
Look, I'm not saying you need to become a swindler yourself. You just need to package it a little nicer, that's all.
Package it?

Yep, like using a ribbon to tie a pretty bow, and putting it in a nice bag...
There we go! Looks much more presentable than before.
You might've already noticed, but there's a huge change coming to the wine racks of Nuova Volsinii.
Used to be that they'd only stock a few types of wine. But now, you can easily find Pinot noirs from Victoria, Cabernet Sauvignons from Columbia, sweet rosés from Bolívar...
It's a miracle for sure, but can you see where the issue lies when you lift up your glass?
This miracle was born from stringent production criteria, and carried all across Terra in cargo containers. They're appropriately priced, and are stable in quality, but what they lack is soul.
Wine isn't meant to lack personality like a fast-food burger! Put those dime-a-dozen industrial goods back on the shelf, and look at the premium gold label Sangiovese in my hand!
The product of craftsmanship honed over decades at a local Siracusan winery! A unique flavor with a lingering aftertaste! One sip will delight the mind, two sips will bring good health—
I'd like one. Will this be enough?
Huh?
Wha?
Aren't you two selling wine? I'm pressed for time, so give it here quick. Err... How do I look?
Ah, er, you look perfectly fine... Where's the fire, signor?
I find myself needing to meet someone, but it's rather last-minute. I didn't expect them to be in Nuova Volsinii, and in my rush, I wasn't able to prepare a gift. Lucky I ran into you.
Grazie mille, signorine. I hope your business goes well.
Signor, wait—Damn, he's fast.
Err... I was only trying to give you an example. Didn't expect there to be anyone crazy enough to actually buy it. Probably a foreigner, since he didn't recognize the wine?
He gave us enough to buy a ton of Verdi...
This is great, though! We finally sold our first bottle! How about a high-five?
But... Mm...
Why the long face? Selling something is a victory, even if it was a misunderstanding. It's his own fault for not studying up...
But he did look like he was really in a rush. Must be a really important meeting?
Hey, kid... If you show up with a bottle of cheap wine in Siracusa... What happens?
—So that's why we're really sorry!
Here's your money back. Please, use it for some other gift. This isn't a high-quality wine, it's just a bottle of—
Verdi, right? So that's why you two were chasing after me in a panic.
You know it?
How could I not, considering all the years I've drank? I was born in Sorrento, and many years ago, I had a falling out with my family. In my anger, I ran off to Columbia.
You can laugh if you want. My Siracusan is a little rusty these days.
But if you knew, then why did you...?
Haha! If I brought a fancy foreign wine as a gift, I'm afraid my papà would slam the door in my face.
The meeting is with your own family?
I didn't know they moved here. I saw them while I was out on the street, nearly didn't recognize them.
What once felt like the biggest deal in all of Siracusa now barely feels important at all. All these years, I had no contact at all. It's time I finally dropped by.
My family was not well-off, so we had Verdi with dinner. I don't know why Papà never tired of it... I hope that once he sees this bottle, he'll let me in.
So there's been no misunderstanding here. A bottle of common, ordinary Verdi, wrapped with care, appeared in front of me precisely when I needed it. And for that, I am willing to pay this price.
If it still weighs on your conscience, then why not offer me a 'good luck' as a bonus?
...Sure! Best of luck to you!
Never thought I'd see the day I'd chase down a buyer to get my product back... You're looking chipper. Happy now?
Mhm! When I tell Nonno, he's gonna say I made a good deal.
Then how about a high-five?
Yay!
No time to rest on your laurels, though. We've only sold one bottle. You can't count on more happy accidents—
Excuse me, are you Bettina?
I am. Who might you be, signore?
Finally found you. Miss Bianca says you sell traditional Siracusan red wine. Is that right?
I'm planning to open a Siracusan restaurant in Victoria, and I might consider bringing a few such items back with me. Could you introduce your product?
Oh, you mean...?

A golden opportunity is knocking, Bettina! Don't just stand there, the important part is putting your marketing skills to good use next! Still remember what I taught you—
Hm.
Signorina Tosia?
Never mind, kid. You... You graduated.
Just forget everything I said. It's better you do things your own way.
Tosia watches the girl and the young man move to the curb, listing out the gains and losses in her head out of habit.

A Siracusan restaurant... Even if he's looking for a local wine, he'd make more profit if he went for something a couple grades higher than Verdi. Well, it's all about what the buyer thinks, in the end.
Just gotta hope he signs a long-term agreement. Though, even if he does, it's still a drop in the bucket. This label isn't going to escape bankruptcy or acquisition that easily...
Hmm?
The conversation nearby seems to pause for a moment. The girl turns to Tosia, jumping and waving her hands, a bright smile plastered all over her face.
Looks like things are going well.
Whatever... As long as she's happy.
One week later.
I've spoken with Mr. Roger, and he approves of your idea. He simply has some hesitation about getting involved, and is worried about the risks.
No rush, the Adeptus Sprawiedliwi isn't making any big moves right now, but this doesn't mean things will go the way G.C.C. planned.
We may be backed by the G.C.C. right now... but we need to make our own preparations.
No matter which of these titans lets something slip through its fingers, we shall enjoy a sumptuous feast.
We are not the only ones waiting to get a slice of the pie. We simply need to be ready, and wait for the perfect wave to carry us aloft...
Ohoho, look who it is! Our shining star of the market finally arrives.
Sales tells me you got quite a few local retailers to sign our shelf display agreement, so I thought we should celebrate!
Thanks. It was just like you said, not much resistance when we were talking.
I meant to have this celebratory dinner yesterday, but my secretary told me you were busy with something?
I made friends with a local girl these past few days. She invited me to her home for dinner. Sorry, I know you don't splurge often...
Why apologize? This is great. We're foreigners in Nuova Volsinii. Only by understanding the Siracusans can we empty their pockets.
It seems my lovely niece has some tricks up her sleeve. You always know exactly why you do things. That's what I like the most about you.
Come, na zdrowie!
I think you've misunderstood something, Wujek Czarek. I didn't go to the kid's place to fish for some information. It was just to sing her 'Happy Birthday'.
Oh, is that so?
The glass filled with first-rate red wine freezes in midair, while the young lady on the other side of the table gives him a smile.
Her family's as ordinary as can be. They even brought all their furniture in from the countryside. A family that's the complete opposite to our 'Nuova Volsinii, Vita Nuova'.
I did manage to get one piece of good news there, though. Look.
Tosia pulls out a soft drink in a glass bottle, resting it on the pure white satin tablecloth. Czarek cannot help but laugh.
You're here to eat dinner, you know. Why bring your own drink?
This is the Chinotto I asked about last week. Her family says there are still grocers in the city who sell it.
I'm not sure if you remember, but my tata often went to Siracusa for work. Every time he came back, he'd bring some snacks and toys for me.
My favorite was this drink, and I'd always beg him to bring more back next time. Haha, it would've been way too heavy, now that I think about it.
Well, you know what happened next. He lost his job, so I didn't get to drink Chinotto anymore, naturally.
Tosia pries off the cap, the soft drink in the brown glass bottle letting out a cheerful hiss.
I've always wanted to try it again. I'm starting to think that if these 'old-fashioned things' really did disappear, it would be a real shame.
Na zdrowie, Wujek Czarek.
Tosia lifts up the bottle, knocking it against the wine glass.
Honestly, that zero-proof sparkling water from last week? Not my cup of tea. No offense.
Lupina, here is the bill of lading for this order of your winery's grapes by Saluzzo Vino.
You can look over the details.

Let me see—
Everything seems to be in order. You're always on top of things.
I'm flattered.
Lupina... there is something which I'm not sure I should ask, in my position.
Why the formality?
Go ahead, Zio Elio. We've known each other for so long.
Ever since Kazimierzian wine entered the market—
You've been running a surplus of grapes at your winery, which has been good for us...
Your prices are reasonable, and it helps us clear inventory. It's a deal that benefits both sides.
Yes... but the amount that you're offering in this batch...
Is it too much for you?
No, no, we use all the grapes we can get. But are you leaving any for your own wine production?
You can tell?
Lupina...
Golden Prairie approached us a little while back.
They offered to buy the Verdi Winery... and they made an offer I couldn't refuse.
The winery is going under, despite our best efforts...
At least Golden Prairie's interest shows that our equipment and vineyards are worth something.
Thank you for everything, Zio Elio. Saluzzo Vino has always been a good partner to the Verdi Winery.
But... what about the other guys? Davide? What about Niccolo? Did he agree?
...I'll convince them.
No, Lupina! How could we sell our Verdi Winery to the Kazimierzians?
Calm down, Niccolo. Let's sit down and talk about this. There's wine, and there's food.
What's that...?
Our signature wine, Sangiovese. You know it well, don't you?
Yes... I remember this label. Old Verdi, your nonno, painted it himself.
I was raising the grapes when he first developed this wine!
Trimmed them vine by vine myself. The clippers were heavy and unwieldy, especially in winter, when you're out all day in the cold.
But it was worth it. These vines are older than all of us put together.
In Kazimierz, they trim their vines with machines, so they can go through a whole vineyard in a single day.
It's not the same. Those stupido machines rip the vines apart. It may save time in the short term, but the grapes don't have long to live once they're done with them.
They don't know how to trim along the grain of the vine, ensuring that the fruits get proper sunlight and develop the right flavor...
You kids don't know the old Siracusan craft, and no one wants to learn anymore.
The Siracusan wine is unique because every vine is as old as the famiglie.
Caring for a grapevine is like caring for family. At least, it was for your nonno.
Niccolo...
Think about it, Lupa. Every grape in Verdi Winery is picked from a vine older than your nonno.
Workers like us have spent our whole lives picking grapes, carrying barrels, making wine.
My son inherited my craft. Even my granddaughter is selling wine for the winery.
Where will we go, if the winery is sold?
I'll make sure everyone is taken care of. Your skills won't go to waste.
I—would the family we've built here still exist, after the winery is sold and all the workers have gone their separate ways?
To me, it's better to die with dignity now, than to continue to try to scrape by in Nuova Volsinii. Give it a decent ending, while this land still has value.
Severance will be paid according to our contract terms.
It's not the severance I'm worried about!
You were never all that interested in running the winery, but don't you feel anything for this place old Verdi kept running all those years?
Nonno wouldn't want his winery to go bankrupt. It's not such a bad thing to find a new home for it. This is Nuova Volsinii, Niccolo, and it's time we accepted the new order.
The old worker stays silent for a while.
Finally, he takes out an invitation from his pocket and puts it on the table.
What's that...?
My granddaughter Betti turns ten next week. We'll do this by the old rules of Siracusa.
She's ten already? I'll have to—
I'm leaving.
At a small, unremarkable home in a quiet alley.
It is already late when Lupina arrives.
A warm light greets her as she opens the door.
I knew I'd find you here.
This is my private bar. You'll always find me here when I'm free.
Here, your usual. One Tramonto with extra orange juice, less syrup, and six cubes of ice.
I thought you'd be busier.
The Kazimierzians' Red Wine Championship is in just a few days. Golden Prairie sent out an invitation to all the local wineries.
We're not really in a position to participate... but I suppose you'll be there?
It's a marketing opportunity, no matter who's organizing it.
Yes, it is an opportunity.
But I've made the necessary arrangements. I don't need to be there personally, for the rest.
You prefer to hide here and mix drinks at your leisure?
Just a little hobby of mine. You have your hobbies too, don't you?
Would you care to check the drum set over there for me, my dear vintner?
She sits down in the drummer's chair and starts banging out a lively rhythm.
Her foot stomps steadily on the cymbal pedal, while the movements of the drumsticks in her hands are clean and confident.
'Se muoio in guerra, seppellitemi con un fiorino, versa le lacrime di mamma, sulla mia tomba come vino...'
A song that every Siracusan child knows. You've brought it to Nuova Volsinii.
An arrangement. The original is too melancholic for this occasion.
The streets are filled with vibrant Kazimierzian wine ads. A Siracusan must learn to read the room.
Maybe not all the time.
Elio told you about our winery.
That's what you're here for.
What's your plan?
The Kazimierzians are coming to audit the assets tomorrow. I've already signed the letter of intent to sell.
There weren't many workers left by the time papá took over from nonno. There's no point in carrying on.
Traditional winemaking methods are time- and labor-intensive. The winery was operating at a loss by the time papá passed it to me.
A shame. But since you've already made your decision—what do you need from me?
It's not like you to hesitate.
The remaining workers... they're all skilled veterans. They'll do well no matter where they go.
Saluzzo Vino has dozens of wineries under your label. There must be places that could use a pair of skilled hands.
I'm not trying to force them on you.
I know the famiglie's rules. You will be doing me a huge favor, one that I'm not in a position to repay.
Just give them a chance, check them out and assign them based on your assessment and needs...
Nothing to be nervous about.
It's only natural that you'd want to take care of your family. And I do need to hire more hands.
...Grazie.
All's well with the workers, but what about you?
Me? I guess I'll... chase my dreams in music?
Frankly, I think I'm a much better drummer than I am a vintner.
The feigned nonchalance is accompanied by a series of drum riffs.
They echo in this little private bar, never leaving the room.
I... can't... I can't just...
Who's there? Elio... you're still here?
Let me help.
It's so quiet... I can hear the ringing in my ears.
This used to be a lively place... the sounds of footsteps, barrels rolling, metal and glass clanging against each other, bubbles sizzling while grapes ferment...
And now, it's all...
There is only silence left.
Lupina slowly walks past the warehouse, the cellar, the vat.
She knows this may be the last time she makes these checks.
Her hand touches the antiquated equipment, the marks of age—
The handle of the presser falls off the screw.
No... the Kazimierzian auditor is coming soon! How could my equipment break at a time like this?!

Oh, this stubborn old stuff... got to screw it back—
Ought to be just like a lightbulb—
It's stuck?
Lupina...
Davide? Good timing! Come, help me fix this thing.
The vertical screw is completely stripped. It won't go back on.
I was just going to tell you, I was doing my regular checks when I found a problem with the filtration system's hydraulic cylinder.
It's cracked and can't maintain hydraulic pressure.
Lupa, the Kazimierzians are here.
A fine classic villa, Signorina Verdi. The wolf's head on the wine barrels is quite detailed, and even the stone tiles in the cellar are tastefully ornamented.
It was my grandfather who painted them.
Shall we discuss what to do with your family's artwork? Would you like us to remove it intact and return it to you, or include it in the purchase?
Remove it?
Since the paintings on the tiles are the work of your late grandfather, we can arrange for an art preservation expert to remove them for you, should you wish. I assure you, they will not be damaged.
Oh, then yes, please.
The expert's fee will be at your own expense, of course.
I knew it... fine, I'll pay. Please make sure the tiles are removed intact and undamaged.
Shall we proceed to the next item?
Alright...
Crusher, fermentation tank, presser, thermostat, filtration system... you have a full complement of winemaking equipment.
Yes, it was my grandfather who procured it. They were the most popular models at the time... very durable.
Your grandfather? That was a while ago, then.
Still, it works well. Please, come and see our crusher.
This machine crushes grapes with minimal loss. My grandfather retrofitted it with extra-wide rollers, increasing production by—
There seems to be an issue with the sealing ring on the machine's connector, if I'm not mistaken?
Equipment assessment is not my specialty, but I am under the impression that the sealing ring should not be exposed.
And your thermostat... I took note of the temperature reading when I passed it. The temperature seems suboptimal for winemaking.
Well... yes, the equipment may be a little old.
But our workers maintain it regularly, and we have all the necessary spare parts on hand. We can get it repaired quickly.
It will not affect delivery.
Ah, if that is what you're concerned about, there is no need to worry.
Your equipment was not included in our initial assessment.
Traditional Siracusan equipment is inefficient and incompatible with our production lines. We did not intend to keep it to begin with. You may dispose of it as you see fit.
This includes the oaken casks in the warehouse that you showed me—
These handmade casks create uncontrolled impurities in the storage process, which are detrimental to quality control for mass-produced wine.
You don't use oaken casks?
We have replaced traditional oaken casks with steel containers, which have better hermetic properties and are more responsive to temperature control.
It'll lose a lot of flavor—
Merda, I sound like my nonno.
That will be a question for our inspector to worry about. I suggest you focus on whether the offer meets your expectations.
I assure you that you have nothing to worry about.
It is the land on which your winery sits that we are interested in. We will offer a fair price for it.
We get a plot of excellent land, while you receive a reasonable payment in turn. It's a win-win arrangement.
I will document the results of the audit, then our legal representative will contact you to finalize the contract.
Please reach out to her if you have any questions.
Would you like to try a sip?
If I recall correctly, we bought out Verdi Winery's inventory last month, as you were in urgent need of liquidity to make payroll.
There will be no need to see me out. Have a nice day, Signorina Verdi.
The Kazimierzian leaves the winery with his briefcase, takes one glance at the lonely vineyard, then gets into a black car that has been waiting for him outside.
It takes a long while, until the sound of the car's engine is long gone, for Lupina to come to her senses.
It's over. Nonno's winery sold, just like that...
I thought... they would care more about our traditions and equipment...
Niccolo.
The presser and crusher, the thermostat and filtration system—
I was the one who broke them.
I know. I'm not here to blame anyone.
You've been here so many years. I doubt you thought breaking a few piece of equipment would stop the purchase.
I just...
Hoped that they would stay?
The pipes... Elio...
He did something else?
I wanted to stop him, but...
I understand your anger... what's done is done. if the auditor didn't find it, there's no reason for us to tell them.
Lupa...
I wasn't much of a businesswoman, but I know how to tell a good guy from a bad one.
That drunk papá of mine wasn't even born when you started working at the winery with my nonno.
You know, he used to measure my height with this presser. See the lines on the cylinder?
It's for the best that it broke. At least it couldn't be sold.
Verdi Winery was my entire life. I watched every new bottle go out the door, saw us weather one storm after another.
I thought my granddaughter, or maybe my grandddaughter's granddaughter, would get to see the new bottles going out... I didn't think it would end this way.
If continuing the old ways won't protect them, maybe this is for the best.
...Is there anything else I can do?
My son would like you to come to his daughter's tenth birthday party.
With a bottle of wine her age, as is tradition.
But—
And take good care of this winery, until it really changes hands, mio caro Lupa.
'My dear vintner, I would very much appreciate if you would pay a visit to my private bar. You may help yourself to my collection.'
He told me to come, but he's nowhere to be found.
People in Siracusa die every day. How's that enough to shut him up at home?
And he wants his guests to mix their own drinks...?
It's been a long time since I've done it... what was it that nonno said?

lines.st: Winemaking is a slow and gradual process. The wine begins to gain its unique flavor during fermentation, like a family slowly brought together.
Sometimes, wines and juices of different flavors are mixed together before being presented for tasting.
No, you're too young to drink.
Are you listening, Lupa?
That's a paintbrush, not a drumstick... I'm not done painting yet—
Yes, you can play with it once I'm done. Look, this is our vineyard. This big wolf head is me, and the small one is you.
You want to paint a couple of brushes too?
Two drumsticks? My, my, mio caro Lupa sure has her own ideas.
You want to be a musician, the most rhythmic drummer on Terra? Then nonno's gonna be the best painter on Terra! Haha!
No, I'm not angry. See? I'm painting right now, on a wine bottle—
I'll take you to the cellar when it gets warmer and decorate the walls. I've wanted to do this for a long time. It took years just for the idea to take shape.
I want you to both inherit the winery, and have the freedom to become a musician.
Your family should not make you give up your dreams.

lines.x: Guess it's come to this, nonno.
I couldn't even come up with a bottle from this year.
Maybe a bit of music to lift the mood?
The drummer walks to the instrument.
There is a finely wrapped gift box on the stool on which she has often sat. She lays down her drumsticks, opens the ribbon-wrapped gift box, and finds a bottle of wine within.
The label features two wolf's heads by the grapevines, one large, one small, with two drumsticks by the ears of the smaller wolf drawn with childish lines.
The label says, 'Verdi 1092'.
The drummer lays her hand on the bottle gently, then puts it back inside the box and takes up the drumsticks. The sound of song begins to echo through the bar.
'Se muoio in guerra, seppellitemi con un fiorino, versa le lacrime di mamma, sulla mia tomba come vino...'
For a long time afterwards, Eirene thought back to her hesitation that night every time she drove her truck alone.

The sky is completely dark by the time the truck stops at the edge of Court Square. She does not turn off the engine; the vibration is transmitted to her wrists via the steering wheel, before gradually subsiding.
She called Lavinia on her way, saying she has something to discuss.
*sigh*
I don't know what to do, Lavinia...
Eirene mutters in the driver's seat, but she cannot bring herself to finish the sentence: 'You're the only one I can count on.'
Is she really the only one? Eirene spends a few moments in bitter silence, as raindrops splash her face through a gap in the window.
She turns off the engine.
I made more money in one trip than I did in the last two weeks combined!
The Kazimierzians pay well.
You showing off?
Make-up payments for this week alone wiped out a whole trip's margin for me.
I don't hear you talking about the heavy fines the Kazimierzians levy.
Hehe, thanks for helping to pay my share. Now that I've gotten paid, how much do I owe you?
Don't worry about it. Brothers help each other out.
Right you are. I'll save a portion and do my part next time someone gets fined.
Saving is the right move. Originium fuel prices are rising. I was just at the station, and boy did it hurt to watch the numbers going up and up and up.
I did run into a bloke from Leoti Pharmacy at the fuel station who lent me his discount card.
I should bring him a pack of smokes next time I go by their shop.
Really? As long as Eirene doesn't catch you hanging out with the wise guy—
Hanging out with who?
No, no, it's nothing.
Ciao, Eirene! Haven't seen you in a while. I think I'm going to break your delivery record soon!
Great. As a reward, you get the transportation security paperwork from the Agenzia per la Sicurezza dei Trasporti.
Hah, anything but the AST! Anyway, it's time for me to go to my next job. A dopo!
He's right, we haven't seen you in camp for a while. How you gotten thinner? You gotta take care of your health, or Sommer will never forgive us—
Don't change the subject. What were you chatting about?
Um, it's nothing, really.
Oh, come on...
When will you and Sam learn?
Where IS Sam, anyway? I didn't see him anywhere in camp, and his schedule's empty for a few days. Where is he?
He's been sick. Fever, vomiting, diarrhea, the whole shebang. Had to go home and lie down after last night's delivery. Gianni's taking his orders for today.
The Kazimierzians dock pay for days off, you know... better to find a sub, if we've got one.
Never mind. I'll get a doctor to look at him.
Did you need him for something?
Eirene irritably shakes the object in her hand. It makes a swishing sound.
The package is obviously wine bottle-shaped, never mind the Saluzzo Vino logo displayed prominently on it.
Why did Saluzzo Vino send us a bottle of wine?
I would have thought that one of you dropped a delivery in the mail room, if the package didn't have Sam's name on it.
Oh, that's probably a moving gift for Sam's cousin's family.
Moving gift?
When his cousin's family first came to Nuova Volsinii, Signor Bellone—I mean, Demetri, helped out.
I think he mentioned he'd send a bottle of wine as a moving gift.
It's just a little wine, Eirene... and it's not for him. Sam quit drinking, you know that.
I know. I'm just wondering how Signor Bellone knew about Sam's cousin.
And you, Ruggiero. I was planning to go shopping at your little supermarket a few days ago, only to find that it's become a Saluzzo Vino outlet.
Since when have you gotten so friendly with each other?
Erm, I rented it to them. Turns out managing a whole supermarket was more trouble than it's worth, and I figured I was better off driving trucks.
Were you in some trouble I didn't know about? Something that you couldn't tell me, but you were comfortable telling the mafia?
It's not that, Eirene...
When will you understand? Small favors are favors too, and all favors have to be repaid someday. With interest.
But they're just helping us right now.
Are they? The Red Wine Championship starts in a few days. Is it not obvious why Saluzzo Vino sent a 'moving gift' right now?
It's 'just a bottle of wine' at this point, but what about later? Mafia money? The famiglia's name? Will you go back to working for them, like you used to?
If you're worried about history repeating itself, I promise you it won't.
Besides, under Nuova Volsinii's new order... even if you don't trust me, you should trust the mayor and Judge Lavinia.
It's not that I don't trust them. It's just...
Never mind. Don't forget what happened at the Carnevale.
Avoid dealing with the famiglie. You may think they're just ordinary employees and shopkeepers, but everything they do is under the watchful eyes of the wise guys.
I know it was traumatic for you, as it was for all of us.
But things have changed for the Saluzzos. Venezia Jr. is gone. It's a new era of leadership—
Ruggiero is interrupted by the sound of his phone ringing. Eirene says nothing; she shakes her head and turns around to leave.
Ruggiero hears an urgent voice as soon as he picks up the phone.
Ruggiero! I can't reach Sam! Wh-What do I do?
Come to the vehicle checkpoint at dock 2! The Kazimierzians say they're slapping on an extra fine, and I just can't get them to listen to me!
What...?
Seeing Ruggiero's anxiety, Eirene gestures for him to pass the terminal.
It's me. What's going on?
Eirene? Oh, I'm so glad you're there!

Sam's been running a fever, so I swapped shifts with him. This run just happened to be on the way to my order. But the Kazimierzians changed the delivery destination at the last minute, and I didn't make it in time.
I tried to explain, but this Kazimierzian doesn't seem to understand what I'm saying. He keeps saying I broke the contract and he's demanding I pay a fine!
Please hurry, Eirene! The print on the contract is tiny and thick and I can't make sense of it!
I'm on my way!
Surely you can make an accommodation? It was your side that changed the delivery address at the last minute. Why should the driver pay a penalty?
Commissioner, all orders are logged in our system, and our adjustments are made according to the published schedule. Drivers bear responsibility for any shift changes they make themselves.
But...
The contract makes it quite clear. Exceptions compromise our ability to enforce our contracts in the future.
Continuing this argument does neither of us any good. If the driver doesn't leave now, based on road conditions and the published schedule...
You may be held in substantive breach of the contract, resulting in a fine equal to fifteen percent of the order.
It will also be your seventh penalty of the month.
Therefore, the windows for any subsequent orders will be tightened accordingly.
Eirene cannot recall what she saw in the forced smile that Gianni offered her.
Was it regret, or apology?
Gianni departed promptly upon hearing the foreign businessman's 'kind words' before Eirene could intervene, muttering a few words of self-encouragement to himself.
I can't just let it go like this, thought Eirene.
Back already, Eirene? How did things go with Gianni?
Did we keep a copy of the Kazimierzian contracts at the camp? Bring it to me.
Wh-What's going on?
The terms... something's not right. There are certain parts that don't seem reasonable. We need to talk it over with their people.
Gianni's trouble hasn't been resolved, has it?
No.
But I'll take care of it.
I knew it.... other drivers have tried to talk to the Kazimierzian. Informally. As for the outcome... I think you can guess.
We were talking about how to handle Gianni's fines while you were away.
His wife just gave birth to twins, and the folks at home are not in the best of health. Thankfully, Deme—

Ruggiero stops in mid-sentence. Eirene asks no more; perhaps she is afraid that she might ask how the mob boss learned about the issues facing Gianni's family, when she herself has only just heard of them moments ago.
She feels like she has spent too long in her office, so long that she can barely recognize her family anymore. Same as it was two years ago.
Get the contract.
I'll be fine. I'll find a way to deal with it.
The AST's drivers do not rely on the kindness of strangers, especially those looking to hide their traps.

The lighting at the Kazimierzian Chamber of Commerce's reception room is much warmer than the Agenzia per la Sicurezza dei Trasporti's office, the thick rug thoroughly muffling the sound of any footsteps.
The water and documents on the table are placed such that one cannot tell if this is the table of a formal negotiation, or simply a courtesy discussion.
The Kazimierzian representative arrive a little earlier than appointed and is looking at the documents when Eirene arrives. He sets the papers down and stands to greet her.
Eirene sits without engaging in small talk.
I wish to make certain adjustments to the cooperation between the Agenzia per la Sicurezza dei Trasporti and the Kazimierzian Chamber of Commerce.
The drivers are not machines. They are doing their best to cooperate. And while it's true they must sometimes be held responsible breaches of contract...
Many more are attributable to a disconnect between contract terms and reality.
Too many of these terms are unreasonable.
Eirene takes out a stack of contracts and pushes them forward. The edges are frayed from excessive flipping, and the pages are heavily labeled.
On their own, the individual terms may not seem unreasonable.
Taken together, however, and they serve to put all the pressure on the lowest rung of the ladder.
The Kazimierzian representative flips through the contract, reading it carefully, staying on one page for minutes, seemingly to confirm the detailed wording.
After some time, he finally puts it away.
I understand your concerns. Indeed, we have also noted the recent freight disruptions.
However, the terms of the contract are clear, and you had the opportunity to review them before you signed it.
Yes, because none of us realized that they would be relevant at the same time, so often.
The rules themselves are not contradictory, it is just that current operating conditions are tighter than expected.
What is your request, then, Commissioner?
I would like more flexibility when dealing with edge cases, at least for the time being. Some space in implementation, if nothing else.
I think it would be conductive to better cooperation in the future.
The Kazimierzian representative is silent for a moment.
Eirene has a feeling that the silence is not a hesitation, but an assessment of whether the statement calls for the dignity of a response.
A fleeting feeling, nothing more.
Marking every single little adjustment would be a considerable burden on management moving forward.
However—
We could, shall we say, set the recent records aside, for the time being.
What do you mean, set aside?
They will not be referenced at the current stage, at least not until this scheduling cycle is over.
What about penalty records of individual drivers?

They will not be scrutinized individually, at the current stage. You may focus your time and energy on ensuring smooth overall operation. Small problems will not be examined so closely when the big picture is secure.
We, too, would prefer that our partners are able to work without pressure.
We recognize, of course, that recent circumstances are exceptional. We appreciate your contributions in dealing with the increased workload associated with the upcoming Red Wine Championship.
Yes, the AST has committed virtually all of our capacity to the Red Wine Championship's orders. I appreciate our Kazimierzian partners' understanding of our drivers' circumstances.
For better cooperation in the future... yes?
I will adjust our schedules and review the conditions of our drivers... I recognize that doing business with you has been very beneficial for our members.

Eirene stands up and shakes hands with her counterpart. The hand held in hers is firm, without applying excessive force, and the expression on the man's face remains polite, exactly as it was when Eirene entered the room.
We will review the next steps once things have settled down a bit.
Eirene nods.
Eirene even feels a slight spring in her step as she leaves the room, carrying the contract.
She did not cede ground. The feeling helps ease the anxiety that she felt before she came, but also causes a pang of regret.
If only she had come sooner to advocate for the drivers. If only she had checked the contract more carefully. Though everything is resolved now—at least, there is room to negotiate.
Eirene spends the next day tallying the violations on all the drivers, the Agenzia per la Sicurezza dei Trasporti's available budget, even her own savings.
Later, she goes back to the camp to tell the others not to worry about the fines.
Everything is getting better, just like the sunny weather that has graced Nuova Volsinii recently, thinks Eirene.
Sam is already feeling better by the time he leaves the pharmacy.
In terms of his wallet, at least. He has been off for three days; his fever has subsided, and he feels ready to go back to work.
Can't have the others subbing in for me all the time... I should figure out my schedule tomorrow, then hit the ground running.
Who's calling at this hour?
Hello?
Oh, Tommaso? From Saluzzo Vino?
Thanks for the flu and fever pills you gave me the other day! They worked great. I was just looking for them in the pharmacy, to keep them on hand for the next time I get a fever.
Oh, you're too kind! You said the order wasn't urgent, but I didn't want to hold up your business any longer, so I took it upon myself to deliver it.
I didn't expect to see medicine boxes in with the pay! You weren't there when I picked it up, but I guess it was you who put the meds in there?
You Saluzzos are too kind—

Oh, sorry, Bellones, of course! You Bellones are too kind! So, what do you need from me at a time like this?
Your boss forgot to add a few crates to the delivery? And no one's available...?
And you need it for tomorrow's Red Wine Championship?
Well, we can't have that! I'm just one block away from your winery, I'll get it! Should only take a few minutes on my bike!
Don't worry about a fee! Neighbors help each other out, after all. You insist? Alright, alright, have it your way. We can talk about it after I deliver the wine!
Heh, guess even the big companies slip up every once in a while.
Good think Tommaso found me... how did he get my number, anyway? Did I ever tell him?
Never mind, that's not important. What IS important is that a Nuova Volsiniese wine wins this Red Wine Championship!
Do the Kazimierzians make good wine? Couldn't possibly be as good as the Siracusan stuff, at any rate...
Two more stops till I get to the venue!
Where did that truck come from?!
Phew...
That driver scared the shit out of me, the way he swerved! Good thing the wine's okay...
Must have dozed off and missed the red light, I guess. Yikes, the whole truck's flipped over. I hope the driver's okay... I should call the police...
Gianni?! Is that you?
Somebody, help! My fratello's hurt! Hey, you—Tommaso! You're here too?
Help me get him out from under the wreck! I'll call an ambulance!
Hello...? Th-There's been a crash! The driver's out cold! I need an ambulance, right now!
...So Tommaso told me their boss will pay for Gianni's medical bills and the truckload of wine.
Said Gianni might not have crashed if they didn't ask me to make the delivery, and the Kazimierzians' stuff wouldn't have spilled...
And then?
Then what? Nothing. That's all Tommaso told me.
It's just an act of kindness, Eirene. Tommaso says the owner of Saluzzo Vino is very troubled about Gianni, that he never expected such a terrible accident.
Besides, Gianni's in hospital, and he needs the money!
You were at the Kazimierzians' place for a while. What are they saying? Do we need to pay compensation for the goods, or is it Saluzzo Vino's responsibility?
The Kazimierzians said they can write off the goods...
Eirene stops mid-sentence. She feels a lump in her throat.
Her gaze falls upon the truck sitting on the edge of the camp. It has not been repaired yet, and the broken glass inside the truck gleams in the sunlight.
The way they put it, they agree to not pursue individual liability for the incident.
It takes a few moments for Sam to process the weight of the message, whereupon he visibly lets out a sigh of relief.
What about Gianni?
No personal restitution.
It'll be treated as a failed contract; they'll write off the loss of goods. Nice words they used, 'sharing risks' and 'treating partners fairly'.
That's great!
Honestly, I don't think Gianni could handle paying restitution. He's got way too much on his plate already.
He's been taking so many jobs lately, the fatigue must have gotten to him...
Anyway, tell the friend who asked you to run the errand that we don't need their help. The AST's insurance will pay part of Gianni's medical bills, and I'll deal with the rest.
Sure, alright! The boys have been talking about chipping in for the bills anyway. I'll do my part too.
Oh, Tommaso, right? I-I'll give him a call now—
Oh, come on...
I doubt the Kazimierzians will let it go so easily. You told us about their nice words. What about the not-so-nice ones?
...They made it very clear that this was an exception that they only agree to based on our current partnership.
What do you mean?
It means that they want us to be more... proactive in working within their system, such as future schedules, routes, and other things that we used to decide on our own.
As for penalty records, they said they'll assess them in aggregate. Bunch of officialese: 'for internal reference only', no direct fines.
That's what they said before too.
Formal renegotiations with the Kazimierzians regarding the specifics will take place after the Red Wine Championship. We won't let them put unreasonable terms into the contract this time...
Anyway, that's all about the truckload of wine. Don't ask questions, and don't think too much about it. It's all in the past now.
Eirene...
I know what you're trying to say.
I don't need it. We don't need it. It's all done.
Don't worry, I'll find a way. Things will get better for drivers at the AST...
For the Truckers' Union.
For a long time afterwards, what Eirene recalls most vividly about those two negotiations is not anything that her counterpart said, but the strange confidence that she had.
She believed—
That things would solve themselves if they were put out in the open, as long as rules and boundaries were upheld, even without having to rely on those forces that she was loathe to involve.
Not now, I don't have time for you—
Eirene impatiently waves away the Lupo deliveryman behind her and turns to face the smartly-dressed Kuranta.
She is anxious yet helpless, unsure what to do with her raised hand.

B-But we couldn't possibly pay such an amount!
And what do you mean, you'll end our partnership if we don't accept...?
Didn't we say the other day...?
Our agreement that day was based on the circumstances before that day. Our demands today are based on the changes that will occur after today.
His tone was calm, impassive, as though he was simply stating an indisputable fact, and was kind enough to explain it again for Eirene's sake.
We will not intervene with the assignment of responsibility for the traffic accident, nor do we intend to influence the judgment of the relevant authorities.
But the destruction of the goods is the outcome, and nothing can change that.
Not to mention the poisoning...
